---
title: "all_args_here(): more examples"
---
<br>

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    error = TRUE,
    collapse = FALSE,
    comment = "##"
)
```
<br>

### Datasets
```{r}
FUN0 <- function(x){ # function with a call written without its package.
    mean(x)
}
FUN1 <- function(x, y){ # function.
    code_for_col <- base::as.vector(
        x = base::unlist(
            x = base::mapply(
                FUN = function(x, y){
                    base::rep(
                        x = y,
                        base::length(x = x)
                    )
                },
                x = x,
                y = y,
                MoreArgs = NULL,
                SIMPLIFY = TRUE,
                USE.NAMES = TRUE
            ),
            recursive = TRUE,
            use.names = TRUE
        ),
        mode = "any"
    )
    # The code below is written without carriage return on purpose.
    code_for_col2 <- base::as.vector(x = base::unlist(x = base::mapply(FUN = function(x, y){base::rep(x = y, base::length(x = x))}, x = x, y = y)))
    middle_bracket <- base::do.call(what = base::c, args = code_for_col)
    middle_bracket2 <- base::do.call(what = base::c, args = code_for_col, quote = FALSE, envir = base::parent.frame())
}
FUN2 <- function(x, y){ # function.
    middle_bracket2 <- base::do.call(
        what = base::c,
        args = code_for_col,
        quote = FALSE,
        envir = base::parent.frame()
    )
}
FUN3 <- function(x, m, d){ # function with calls that cannot be fully corrected.
    a <- base::matrix(x, ncol = 2) # base::matrix() tests missing(nrow)
    b <- base::diag(x) # base::diag() counts its arguments with nargs()
    e <- stats::t.test(formula = y ~ g, data = d) # the method is chosen from the formula, x not written
    f <- base::round(x) # round.POSIXt(), method for date-times, has no digits argument
    base::rownames(m) <- base::paste0("r", 1:2) # target of an assignment
}
# Folder where the files are written.
tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(), fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
```
<br>

### Simple examples
```{r}
# Example that returns an error: the calls must be written with their package (see colons_check()).
saferDev::all_args_here(
    x = FUN0,
    table_export = FALSE,
    fun_export = FALSE,
    out_path = NULL,
    df_name = "res.tsv",
    overwrite = FALSE,
    safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = ""
)

# Example indicating missing arguments, and returning the modified function.
saferDev::all_args_here(
    x = FUN2,
    table_export = FALSE,
    fun_export = FALSE,
    out_path = NULL,
    df_name = "res.tsv",
    overwrite = FALSE,
    safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = ""
)
```
<br>

### Empty values and corrections not applied
The default value of `nrow` is not written into the `base::matrix()` call, because `base::matrix()` tests `missing(nrow)`: `nrow` gets an empty value, which keeps the result. The other calls are left unchanged, and listed with their reason in the `CORRECTIONS NOT APPLIED` message: `base::diag()` uses `nargs()`, `x = ` added to `stats::t.test()` would change the method used, `digits = 0` added to `base::round()` would fail for date-times, and `base::rownames()` is the target of an assignment:
```{r}
saferDev::all_args_here(
    x = FUN3,
    table_export = FALSE,
    fun_export = FALSE,
    out_path = NULL,
    df_name = "res.tsv",
    overwrite = FALSE,
    safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = ""
)
```
Likewise, `graphics::plot(x)` and `graphics::plot(x = x)` are listed under `CORRECTIONS NOT APPLIED`, because the methods of `plot()` name their arguments differently: `plot.formula()` names the first one `formula`, and an added `y = ` would match `ylim` and `ylab` of `plot.table()`.
<br>

### Arguments <code>table_export</code>, <code>out_path</code>, <code>df_name</code> and <code>overwrite</code>
```{r}
# Write the table into the res.tsv file of the tempo_dir folder,
# and overwrite res.tsv if it already exists in this folder.
saferDev::all_args_here(
    x = FUN2,
    table_export = TRUE,
    fun_export = FALSE,
    out_path = tempo_dir,
    df_name = "res.tsv",
    overwrite = TRUE,
    safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = ""
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>fun_export</code>: return or write the modified function
When arguments are missing, `all_args_here()` returns the modified function (the missing arguments being inserted as proposed in the `$STATUS` column of the table), or writes it into a `.R` file named with the name of the submitted function and `_safer` added at the end:

```{r}
# Returns the modified function, or NULL if nothing has to be modified.
FUN2_safer <- saferDev::all_args_here(
    x = FUN2,
    table_export = FALSE,
    fun_export = FALSE,
    out_path = NULL,
    df_name = "res.tsv",
    overwrite = FALSE,
    safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = ""
)
FUN2_safer # modified function.

# Write the modified function into the FUN2_safer.R file of the tempo_dir folder.
saferDev::all_args_here(
    x = FUN2,
    table_export = FALSE,
    fun_export = TRUE,
    out_path = tempo_dir,
    df_name = "res.tsv",
    overwrite = TRUE,
    safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = ""
)
```
When `fun_export = TRUE`, the modified function is not returned, but written into the file. No file is written if nothing is corrected.
<br>

### Argument <code>safer_check</code>
```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# Safer checks are performed before running the main code.
saferDev::all_args_here(
    x = FUN2,
    table_export = FALSE,
    fun_export = FALSE,
    out_path = NULL,
    df_name = "res.tsv",
    overwrite = FALSE,
    safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = ""
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>lib_path</code>
```{r}
# The "NOTGOOD" path does not exist.
saferDev::all_args_here(
    x = FUN2,
    table_export = FALSE,
    fun_export = FALSE,
    out_path = NULL,
    df_name = "res.tsv",
    overwrite = FALSE,
    safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = "NOTGOOD",
    error_text = ""
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>error_text</code>
```{r}
# Add a text in error messages returned by all_args_here().
saferDev::all_args_here(
    x = FUN2,
    table_export = FALSE,
    fun_export = FALSE,
    out_path = NULL,
    df_name = "res.tsv",
    overwrite = FALSE,
    safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = "NOTGOOD",
    error_text = " === TEXT ADDED ==="
)
```
<br>

### All the arguments
```{r}
saferDev::all_args_here(
    x = FUN1, # R function.
    table_export = FALSE, # write the table into a file?
    fun_export = FALSE, # write the modified function into a .R file?
    out_path = NULL, # folder where the files are written (required if table_export or fun_export is TRUE).
    df_name = "res.tsv", # name of the file of the table.
    overwrite = FALSE, # overwrite the files already existing in out_path?
    safer_check = TRUE, # perform some "safer" checks (see https://github.com/safer-r)?
    lib_path = NULL, # where the required packages are if not in the default directories.
    error_text = "" # add information in error messages returned by the function.
)
```
